newsitem.title: USA: Warmer, dry weekend forecast for U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Warmer, dry weekend forecast for U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Warmer, dry weather was forecast for much of the U.S. Midwest this weekend which should allow for rapid soybean harvest progress, meteorologists said.
"As far as the corn belt is concerned, you're looking at pretty favorable harvest conditions," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express.
Friday morning brought cold temperatures to northern Illinois, Indiana and Ohio with the freeze line extending from Springfield, Ill., through South Bend, Ind. and Findlay, Ohio, Gesser said.
Temperatures were expected to warm into the 50s Farenheit across much of the corn belt Friday with some 60s F possible in southern portions of the belt.
Highs Saturday were expected in the 60s F to 70s F in the south. No major precipitation was forecast with the warm-up.
Another cold front was seen moving in Sunday but forecasting models indicated it would not get as cold as previously expected, Gesser said.
"It looks like we'll have a cold front every two to 2-1/2 days but not a lot of precipitation," Gesser said.
But temperatures should average near normal to slightly above normal as the cold fronts move out quickly and warmer air settles in, he said.
